question: Who among the following is NOT considered a leader of the Moderates in the Indian National Congress? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Ferozshah Mehta
Dadabhai Naoroji
Aurobindo Ghosh
Gopal Krishna Gokhale
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Aurobindo Ghosh

Explanation:
In the early phase of the Indian National Congress, the Moderates were leaders who adopted a conciliatory approach towards British rule. Prominent among them were Dadabhai Naoroji, Ferozshah Mehta, and Gopal Krishna Gokhale. They sought reforms through constitutional means. In contrast, Aurobindo Ghosh belonged to the Extremist or Garam Dal faction, which advocated a more aggressive nationalist stance. He promoted Swadeshi, boycott, and national education. Hence, he is not considered a Moderate leader.

question: When were privy purses officially abolished in India? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: 1956
1969
1971
1980
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1971

Explanation:
Privy purses in India were officially abolished in 1971 through the 26th Constitutional Amendment, which came into effect on 28 December 1971. The privy purse was an annual payment made to former rulers of princely states in exchange for their agreement to merge their territories with the Indian Union. The Indira Gandhi government first attempted to abolish them in 1969, but the Supreme Court struck down the order. Subsequently, the Parliament passed the 26th Amendment in 1971, which removed the constitutional recognition of princely privileges and privy purses. The move was aimed at promoting social and economic equality and abolishing feudal privileges. The amendment also deleted Articles 291 and 362 from the Constitution, which had provided for the privy purse.

question: What was the main reason for the protest against the Simon Commission in 1928? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Introduction of new laws
Lack of Indian representation
High taxes
Discrimination against minorities
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Lack of Indian representation

Explanation:
The Simon Commission was sent to India in 1928 to review constitutional reforms. However, it faced widespread protests because the commission had no Indian members. Indians saw this as a violation of their right to self-determination and an insult to their nationality. The slogan 'Simon Go Back' became popular. During a protest in Lahore, Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a police lathi charge. This protest marked a significant phase in the Indian independence movement.

question: The Poligars rebelled against the British in which Presidency, when the British tried to snatch away their military and land rights? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 3)

The Poligars fiercely resisted British encroachment on their traditional rights and autonomy.

question: In which year was the Partition of Bengal, initially implemented by the British in 1905, officially annulled? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (06/06/2025) Shift 3)
options: 1909
1910
1916
1911
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1911

Explanation:
The Partition of Bengal was implemented in 1905 by Lord Curzon, dividing Bengal into East and West regions. This decision faced strong opposition from Indian nationalists, leading to the Swadeshi and Boycott movements. Under increasing political pressure and during the Delhi Durbar of 1911, the British government decided to annul the partition. On December 12, 1911, King George V announced the revocation of the Partition of Bengal at the Delhi Durbar. Simultaneously, the capital of British India was shifted from Kolkata to Delhi. Thus, the Partition of Bengal was officially annulled in 1911.

question: Which reformer gave the slogan 'One God, One Caste'? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (12/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Dayanand Saraswati
Jyotiba Phule
Keshub Chandra Sen
Narayana Guru
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Narayana Guru

Explanation:
Narayana Guru (1855-1928) was a great social reformer and spiritual leader from Kerala who fought against the caste system and social inequality. His famous slogan was "One God, One Caste" (Eka Jati, Eka Deivam), emphasizing the equality of all human beings. He established a temple at Aruvippuram and opened it for all castes, defying traditional restrictions. He believed that there is only one God and one caste, and the differences in caste are man-made. His teachings promoted unity and brotherhood in society. In contrast, Dayanand Saraswati gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas," Jyotiba Phule worked for the upliftment of Shudras and women, and Keshub Chandra Sen was associated with Brahmo Samaj.

एकीकरण के बाद राजकुमारों को दी जाने वाली पेंशन

solution_hi:

Explanation:
'प्रिवी पर्स' भारतीय राजाओं को उनके राज्यों के भारत में विलय के बाद दी जाने वाली वार्षिक पेंशन थी। यह व्यवस्था 1947 में स्वतंत्रता के बाद की गई थी, जिसमें रियासतों के शासकों को उनकी उपाधियाँ और कुछ विशेषाधिकार बनाए रखने की अनुमति थी। 1971 में 26वें संविधान संशोधन द्वारा प्रिवी पर्स को समाप्त कर दिया गया, जिससे रियासतों का विशेष दर्जा भी खत्म हुआ। यह कदम तत्कालीन प्रधानमंत्री इंदिरा गांधी के नेतृत्व में उठाया गया था।

question: The Mahalwari system was prevalent in certain regions of northern and central India. From whom was the land revenue collected under the Mahalwari system? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Religious institutions
Village head
Landlords
Individual peasants
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Village head

Explanation:
The Mahalwari system was proposed by Holt Mackenzie in 1822 and later implemented by William Bentinck. Under this system, the entire village or mahal was treated as a unit for revenue assessment. The village head or lambardar was responsible for collecting revenue from the villagers and depositing it with the British. This system was prevalent mainly in the North-Western Provinces, Punjab, and Central India. The revenue rate was based on soil fertility and produce, typically ranging from 50% to 75% of the total yield. Peasants did not own the land but only cultivated it, while the village head acted as an intermediary between the British and the cultivators.

☛ When was the Mahalwari system implemented? → 1833
☛ What was the village chief called? → Lambardar

☛ Which regions had the Mahalwari system? → North-Western Provinces, Punjab, Central India
question_hi: महालवाड़ी व्यवस्था उत्तरी और मध्य भारत के कुछ क्षेत्रों में प्रचलित थी। महालवाड़ी व्यवस्था के अंतर्गत भूमि राजस्व किससे वसूला जाता था? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1)

जमींदार
व्यक्तिगत किसान

Explanation:
महालवाड़ी व्यवस्था 1822 में होल्ट मैकेंज़ी द्वारा प्रस्तावित और बाद में विलियम बेंटिक द्वारा लागू की गई थी। इस प्रणाली में पूरे गाँव या महाल को इकाई मानकर राजस्व तय किया जाता था। ग्राम प्रधान या लंबरदार पूरे गाँव की ओर से राजस्व वसूल करता था और अंग्रेजों को जमा करता था। यह व्यवस्था मुख्यतः उत्तर-पश्चिमी प्रांतों, पंजाब और मध्य भारत में प्रचलित थी। राजस्व की दर भूमि की उर्वरता और उपज के आधार पर तय की जाती थी, जो आमतौर पर कुल उपज का 50% से 75% तक होती थी। इस प्रणाली में किसानों को भूमि का स्वामित्व नहीं मिलता था, बल्कि वे केवल खेती करते थे।

question: Which of the following key centres of the 1857 Revolt was recaptured from the rebel forces in September 1857? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1)

Explanation:

question: The revolt of 1857 broke out on 10th May from which of the following places, when sepoys rose in rebellion and marched towards Delhi to restore Bahadur Shah II to the throne? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Awadh
Meerut
Kanpur
Mysore
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Meerut

Explanation:
The Revolt of 1857 began on May 10, 1857, at Meerut. The immediate cause was the use of greased cartridges, rumored to contain cow and pig fat, which offended both Hindu and Muslim soldiers. 85 sepoys at Meerut refused to use the cartridges and were imprisoned. On May 10, fellow sepoys revolted, broke the jail, and freed their comrades. They then marched to Delhi and declared Bahadur Shah II as their leader. The revolt spread across northern India but was eventually suppressed by the British. Meerut's role as the starting point makes it a key location in Indian history.

☛ What British historians call the 1857 Revolt → Sepoy Mutiny

question: During the colonial period, India's industrial development was the result of British policies. Which of the following options best describes the nature of industrial development in India at the eve of independence? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: Balanced regional distribution of heavy industries
Strong domestic capital goods industry in all provinces
Widespread industrial growth across rural and urban areas
Limited industrial activity, mainly concentrated in a few cities like Calcutta and Bombay
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Limited industrial activity, mainly concentrated in a few cities like Calcutta and Bombay

Explanation:
During the colonial period, British policies were designed to keep India as a supplier of raw materials and a market for finished goods. This resulted in a limited and unbalanced industrial development. Heavy industries were discouraged, and only light industries like textiles were allowed to grow. These industries were concentrated in port cities such as Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras, which were convenient for export and import. Rural areas saw almost no industrial growth. By the time of independence, India had a very narrow industrial base, with most activity limited to a few urban centers. This pattern of limited, concentrated industrialization is best described by Option 4.

☛ Reason for industrial growth after WWI → War demand and reduced imports
☛ Major iron and steel company established in 1907 → Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO)

question_hi: औपनिवेशिक काल के दौरान, भारत का औद्योगिक विकास ब्रिटिश नीतियों का परिणाम था। स्वतंत्रता की पूर्व संध्या पर भारत में औद्योगिक विकास की प्रकृति का सबसे अच्छा वर्णन करने वाला निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा विकल्प है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)

Explanation:
औपनिवेशिक काल में ब्रिटिश नीतियों ने भारत के औद्योगिक विकास को सीमित और असंतुलित बना दिया। अंग्रेज भारत को कच्चे माल का स्रोत और तैयार माल का बाजार बनाना चाहते थे, जिससे भारी उद्योगों का विकास नहीं हो पाया। जो उद्योग विकसित हुए वे मुख्यतः हल्के उद्योग थे, जैसे कपड़ा, और ये कलकत्ता, बॉम्बे, मद्रास जैसे बंदरगाह शहरों में केंद्रित थे। देहाती क्षेत्रों में औद्योगिक विकास लगभग नहीं के बराबर था। परिणामस्वरूप, स्वतंत्रता की पूर्व संध्या पर भारत में औद्योगिक गतिविधि बहुत सीमित थी और कुछ शहरों तक ही सिमटी हुई थी।

question: The Nizam of Hyderabad tried to project his rule as: (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)
options: a Muslim sovereignty in Deccan
a British protectorate
a Hindu monarchy
a secular republic
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is a Muslim sovereignty in Deccan

Explanation:
The Nizam of Hyderabad tried to project his rule as a Muslim sovereignty in Deccan. After the decline of the Mughal Empire, the Nizam emerged as an independent ruler and liked to be called the "true emperor of Deccan". He promoted Islamic traditions and Persian culture, linking his rule with Muslim identity. Although Hyderabad was a British protectorate, the Nizam maintained autonomy in internal affairs and emphasized his sovereignty. As a Muslim ruler in a Hindu-majority region, he presented an image of Muslim sovereignty. His state had its own currency, army, and postal system, reinforcing this projection.

question_hi: हैदराबाद के निज़ाम ने अपने शासन को किस रूप में प्रस्तुत करने का प्रयास किया? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (13/06/2025) Shift 2)

एक ब्रिटिश संरक्षित राज्य

Solution: सही उत्तर है दक्षिण में एक मुस्लिम संप्रभुता

हैदराबाद के निज़ाम ने अपने शासन को दक्षिण भारत में एक स्वतंत्र मुस्लिम संप्रभुता के रूप में प्रस्तुत करने का प्रयास किया। निज़ाम मुगल साम्राज्य के पतन के बाद एक स्वतंत्र शासक के रूप में उभरे और अपनी रियासत को "दक्खन का असली बादशाह" कहलवाना पसंद करते थे। उन्होंने इस्लामी परंपराओं और फारसी संस्कृति को बढ़ावा दिया और अपने शासन को मुस्लिम पहचान से जोड़ा। हालांकि हैदराबाद ब्रिटिश संरक्षित राज्य था, निज़ाम ने आंतरिक मामलों में स्वायत्तता बनाए रखी और अपनी संप्रभुता पर जोर दिया। वे हिंदू बहुल आबादी वाले क्षेत्र में मुस्लिम शासक थे, इसलिए उन्होंने मुस्लिम संप्रभुता की छवि प्रस्तुत की।

question: Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement after the violent incident at Chauri Chaura. In which present-day state is Chauri Chaura located? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)

Bihar

question: Commercial crops were prioritised over food crops during colonial rule. Which of the following is an example of a commercial crop promoted by the British? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)
options: Indigo
Millets
Wheat
Rice
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Indigo

Explanation:
During colonial rule, the British prioritized commercial crops over food crops. These crops were used for export and as raw materials for industries. Indigo was a major commercial crop used for dyeing textiles. British authorities forced Indian farmers to cultivate indigo, which led to a decline in food production. In contrast, millets, wheat, and rice were primarily food crops. Indigo cultivation was mainly concentrated in Bihar and Bengal and formed a significant part of British exports. The exploitation of indigo farmers led to the Indigo Revolt in 1859-60.

question_hi: औपनिवेशिक शासन के दौरान खाद्य फसलों पर व्यावसायिक फसलों को प्राथमिकता दी गई थी। निम्नलिखित में से कौन सा ब्रिटिश द्वारा प्रचारित एक व्यावसायिक फसल का उदाहरण है? (RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I (14/06/2025) Shift 1)

बाजरा
गेहूँ
चावल
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है नील

Explanation:
औपनिवेशिक शासन के दौरान ब्रिटिशों ने खाद्य फसलों की जगह व्यावसायिक फसलों को बढ़ावा दिया। इन फसलों का उपयोग निर्यात और उद्योगों में कच्चे माल के रूप में होता था। नील एक प्रमुख व्यावसायिक फसल थी, जिसका उपयोग कपड़ों को रंगने के लिए किया जाता था। ब्रिटिशों ने भारतीय किसानों को नील की खेती के लिए मजबूर किया, जिससे खाद्यान्न उत्पादन प्रभावित हुआ। इसके विपरीत, बाजरा, गेहूँ और चावल मुख्यतः खाद्य फसलें थीं। नील की खेती मुख्यतः बिहार और बंगाल में होती थी और यह ब्रिटिश निर्यात का महत्वपूर्ण हिस्सा थी।
